Rise and Reclaim brings together lived experience, expert insight and practical guidance to support people at every stage of their recovery journey. Each episode explores a different dimension of rebuilding life after abuse, from confidence and identity, to friendship, finances, careers and finding your way back to yourself.
This is not a podcast about surviving. It is about what comes next.
Rise and Reclaim is proudly brought to you by Verdella, the online domestic violence recovery program designed to support victim survivors in practical and meaningful ways. Verdella is available through licensing partnerships with employers and community service organisations committed to supporting recovery and wellbeing. To find out more, visit verdella.com.au.
Because recovery is not something anyone should have to navigate alone.

title: The Connected Horse
author: Amie willson
description:
The Connected Horse is an educational podcast exploring the evolving world of equine health, performance, rehabilitation and long-term horse care. Each episode brings together practical insights from veterinary professionals, rehabilitation specialists, farriers, nutritionists and other members of the equine care team to explore how better communication, evidence-informed decision-making and whole-horse thinking can improve outcomes.The series focuses on the idea that excellent horse care is rarely the responsibility of one person alone.

From recognising early changes in movement and performance to understanding rehabilitation, preventative management and the role of objective assessment, listeners will discover how different professionals can work together around the individual needs of each horse. For professionals looking to deepen their knowledge, equine courses can provide an additional educational pathway for developing practical understanding and staying informed about evolving approaches to equine care.The podcast complements the philosophy behind My Apeiron Care, which brings together expertise across equine sports medicine, advanced diagnostics, rehabilitation and multidisciplinary professional collaboration.

My Apeiron Care describes its approach as moving beyond reactive intervention toward structured management, prevention and sustained wellbeing, supported by connected care pathways.Each episode aims to make complex equine-care topics accessible without oversimplifying them. Rather than providing individual veterinary advice, The Connected Horse encourages listeners to ask better questions, understand the roles of different professionals and appreciate the importance of coordinated care throughout a horse's life and career.

My name is Peter Sinodinos. Over the years I’ve had the privilege of working closely with leaders, boards and organisations, observing what helps people and organisations perform at their best and what can get in the way.


I’ve also written and contributed to broader conversations about leadership, people and strategy, including my book Leadership: Ideas, People and Strategy, as well as work exploring governance, board effectiveness and organisational performance.


But The Boardroom Test isn't really about titles, credentials or my background. It’s about experience, and what that experience has taught me about the people and dynamics behind important decisions, because what really happens when the doors close and the boardroom begins ?


Behind the board papers, presentations and formal agendas are people. People with different experiences, perspectives, personalities and ambitions. People who have to build trust, challenge one another, navigate disagreement and, ultimately, make decisions that can have significant consequences.


The Boardroom Test is a 13-part journey into those dynamics.

Across 13 conversations, we explore leadership, judgement, governance, influence, courage, conflict, accountability and the relationships that shape decision-making when the stakes are high and the answers aren't always obvious.


We'll explore how to challenge without undermining, disagree without becoming disagreeable, listen when you think you already know the answer, and have the difficult conversations that leaders sometimes avoid.


Most importantly, we'll explore what it really takes to navigate the boardroom, not just to have a seat at the table, but to make a meaningful contribution when it matters.


Because being in the room is one thing.


Passing the Boardroom Test is another.


13 conversations. 13 perspectives. One question:


When the decision really matters, how do you show up?

description:
Welcome to The AscendED School a podcast for school leaders, educators, and anyone committed to building schools that prepare students not just for graduation, but for life beyond the K–12 environment.

Hosted by experienced educators and school leaders Rebecca Burtram, Adam Howard, and Bruce MacBain, The AscendED School brings together decades of experience from the classroom, school administration, and educational leadership.

Our guiding belief is simple:

Students should be prepared, not just promoted.

We believe effective preparation requires schools to have systems in place to meet the needs of today. 

We believe students deserve adults who expect great things from them and who provide the structures, relationships, instruction, and support necessary to help them meet those expectations.

On each episode, we explore the real challenges facing schools today, including:

* Student behavior and school culture
* Accountability and restorative practices
* Teacher support and retention
* School leadership and systems
* Student engagement and motivation
* Preparing students for life after graduation
* Building cultures of high expectations and high support
* Moving from individual solutions to schoolwide systems
* Creating schools where both adults and students can thrive

We don't believe there are easy answers. And we don't believe that schools should have to choose between relationships and accountability, support and expectations, or compassion and consequences.

Instead, we ask a different question:

What systems do schools need to help students become the people they need to be beyond K–12?

Join us as we challenge conventional thinking, share lessons from the field, and explore practical strategies that school leaders can put into action.

The goal isn't simply to get students across the graduation stage.
The goal is to make sure they're ready for what comes after it.

Amor y pedagogía de Miguel de Unamuno es una novela original, irónica y profundamente crítica que explora el choque entre la razón abstracta y la vida humana real.
La obra gira en torno a don Avito Carrascal, un hombre obsesionado con aplicar principios científicos y pedagógicos a la formación de su hijo. Convencido de que el genio puede fabricarse mediante métodos racionales y educación cuidadosamente planificada, intenta controlar todos los aspectos de la vida del niño desde su nacimiento.
Sin embargo, Unamuno muestra cómo ese proyecto entra en conflicto con la naturaleza humana, los sentimientos, la libertad individual y las contradicciones de la existencia. A través de situaciones a veces cómicas y a veces trágicas, la novela cuestiona la fe ciega en el positivismo, la educación mecánica y la idea de que la vida puede reducirse a fórmulas.
Con un estilo agudo y reflexivo, Amor y pedagogía combina sátira, filosofía y drama para examinar temas como la paternidad, la identidad, la inteligencia, el amor y el sentido de la vida.
Este audiolibro es una excelente elección para quienes disfrutan de la literatura española, la novela filosófica, la sátira intelectual, Miguel de Unamuno y las obras que enfrentan razón y emoción.

title: E.T.H.A.N
author: Olldun
description:
When I was growing up, some of my favorite memories were listening to my grandfather tell stories. He had a way of making faraway places feel close and turning simple moments into adventures.

At the time, I thought he was just telling great stories. Looking back, I realize he was also passing down our culture, our family history, and a curiosity about the world.

Years later, when I became a dad, I wanted to give my son, Ethan, that same feeling.

That’s how E.T.H.A.N. — Every Tale Holds A New Adventure began.

Each episode is an adventure Ethan and I take together. We explore different parts of the world through folktales, legends, and stories that families have shared for generations. Along the way, we learn about the people and places behind the stories, discover fun facts, and talk about the lessons each tale can teach us.

Think of it as a modern family campfire—something you can listen to in the car, before bed, around the breakfast table, or anytime you want to slow down and spend a little time together.

And the adventure doesn’t have to end when the episode does.

Our hope is that each story inspires your family to keep exploring—cook something new, send a postcard, ask a grandparent about their childhood, or simply have a conversation together.

Because childhood goes by quickly, and often the moments our kids remember most are the simple ones we share with them.

So bring your family, bring your curiosity, and come explore the world with Ethan and me—one story at a time.

And remember, Ethan…

Every Tale Holds A New Adventure.

title: The Data Centre MRO Gap and the Cost of Downtime
author: Marc Cudd
description:
Episode Summary:

 

The UK is now home to more than 520 data centres, with continued growth driven by demand for AI. While planning and energy grid capacity dominate the conversation, maintenance, repair and operations procurement (MRO) - the work that keeps facilities running once they go live - is talked about far less. Yet when a data centre goes down, the impact is immediate: downtime cost, reputational damage, operational disruption, and a strain on already limited engineering resources.

 

Hosted by RS UK & Ireland, this episode brings together the expertise of the Chartered Institute of Procurement & Supply (CIPS) and the Data Centre Alliance (DCA) for an essential conversation on business-critical issues in the sector that aren't discussed nearly enough:

 

  • What happens when a data centre moves from construction into live operation
  • Why handover is such a critical moment
  • And how operators, procurement teams and suppliers can be better prepared for the demands of live operation

 

Featuring:

 

Navid Mehr, Executive and Board Member, The Data Centre Alliance (DCA)

Phil Broughton, Business Development Leader, Chartered Institute of Procurement & Supply (CIPS)

Richard Graham, Industry Sector Manager, RS UK & Ireland

 

Host: Ashley Norris, Wearevolume.io

 

For more information, visit the RS Data Centres Hub

author: Cristian Sylvestre / David Pope
description: Much of what is “new” in safety has not been proven to make any difference to safety performance, some of it possibly making it worse. Our aim is to use legitimate science to explore ways to help improve safety and move beyond just fixing the environment or improving the system or making safety more conscious.These three approaches helped us improve safety and brought us to where we are today, but they are struggling to help us improve further.In the Safety Frontiers Podcast, our focus is to explore novel ways of thinking about safety: using different approaches to make systems more effective, strengthen safety culture, and take a deep dive into the discoveries and insights gained from neurobiology and brain research over the last 5 years. This will be new information to many. We know disruptive thinking challenges long-held beliefs and accepted norms. As such, it could be confronting for some. However, significant improvements tend to come from new perspectives and that is what we are interested in.We do not advocate one approach over another, we are here to explore new safety frontiers, to ensure that we are using everything available to help people with safety.
